title: Resilience integration campaign brief - SLO adoption & cross-team rollout
content:
Purpose
This brief defines a compact, cross-functional campaign to integrate Service Level Objectives (SLOs) into product roadmaps and operational practices across Redwood Inference. The goal is pragmatic: get customer-impacting services instrumented with meaningful SLIs, adopt a lightweight SLO taxonomy, and establish rollout gates and runbooks so teams can own reliability without heavy central coordination.

Scope & Focus Areas
- Scope: initial campaign covers three service families with high customer impact and diverse topologies: Hosted API (multi-tenant REST surface), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + autoscaling), Private (VPC/on-prem control plane).
- Focus areas: SLI definition & measurement, telemetry consumption and dashboards, alert/runbook alignment, release gating and rollouts, stakeholder onboarding and success metrics.

Success criteria (end of Q3 2026)
- 80% of prioritized endpoints have production SLIs and a declared SLO with owner assigned.
- SLO scorecards (weekly cadence) published to Console dashboards for Hosted API and Dedicated.
- At least two automatic fallback policies tied to SLO breach signals successfully exercised in canary.
- On-call runbooks and escalation paths for SLO breaches exist for every onboarded service.

High-level timeline (12 weeks)
- Week 0-2: Intake & taxonomy alignment — finalize SLI candidates, measurement instrumentation plan, and measurement buckets (latency P50/P95, availability, error-rate, cold-start tail).
- Week 3-6: Instrumentation sprint — telemetry switches, per-route metrics, prefixes for KV-cache hits, per-tenant token-level cost hooks where feasible.
- Week 7-8: Validation & rollup — QA signals, define SLOs, compute burn-rate models, map noise sources.
- Week 9-10: Runbook & automation — create runbooks, alert thresholds, paging flows, and automated mitigation actions (traffic-tier routing, model-fallback).
- Week 11-12: Canary & measure — run a production canary with SLO monitoring enabled, exercise fallback and rollback flow, publish playbook.

Roles & responsibilities
- Campaign lead (SRE): Asha Mehta — program coordination, SLO taxonomy, instrumentation standards.
- Product liaison (Hosted API): Sofia Martinez — prioritize endpoints, product acceptance criteria, customer comms.
- Infra/Platform: Ravi Patel — metrics pipelines, sampling, retention and tag schemas.
- Observability/Console: Elena Zhou — dashboards, scorecards, alerting templates.
- Solutions & CS: Marcus Bell — identify customers for pilot, collect success criteria and runbook sign-off.
- Engineering teams (service owners): provide API surface lists, own SLO targets, implement non-blocking instrumentation changes.

SLO Taxonomy & Guiding Principles
- Minimal viable SLO: choose one primary SLI per service (availability or latency) plus one secondary (error-rate or quality/regression indicator). Keep targets realistic to avoid noisy paging.
- Consumer-centric: define SLIs in terms of user-visible outcomes (client response success, request latency at the API boundary), not internal queue depths.
- Tiered SLOs: differentiate internal platform SLOs vs. external customer-facing SLOs; use different burn-rate tolerances for internal tooling.
- Simplicity first: begin with coarse buckets (P50/P95 latency, 99.9% availability) and iterate when signal quality justifies finer granularity.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum for each onboarded endpoint)
- Unique route ID and route tags (product, tenant-type, model-family).
- Success/failure counters with error taxonomy (client, model, infra).
- Latency histograms with streaming-friendly buckets.
- Prefix/KV cache hit metrics for generation endpoints.
- Request sampling for traces (1-5%) with correlated token counts for cost analysis.

Telemetry & pipeline requirements
- Metric cadence: 1s or 10s aggregation for latency; 1m rollup to long-term store.
- Tag schema: service, route_id, model_variant, region, tenant_tier. Platform infra to enforce tag schema during ingestion.
- Retention: raw 14d, rollup 90d, scorecard inputs downsampled to 1h for 1y.
- Cost/efficiency metrics: token-usage per request, GPU occupancy signals for Dedicated pools.

Alerting & Runbooks
- Alert types: SLO burn-rate (primary), SLI trend divergence (emerging regressions), telemetry pipeline gaps.
- Alert behavior: initial alert to service owner; if burn-rate persists for >30 min, escalate to platform on-call.
- Runbooks: for each service include: how to identify incident class, triage checklist, mitigation steps (e.g., route to cheaper model variant, enable cached responses, scale Dedicated pool), rollback criteria, post-mortem ownership.

Rollout gates & risk controls
- Instrumentation gate: no canary until route-level metrics pass QA (no negative sampling bias, correct tags).
- Canary gate: exercise fallback policies in a controlled subset (1-5% traffic). Canary must demonstrate that automatic fallback reduces burn by >= 50% in test simulations.
- Release gate: product sign-off that customer-visible behavior is acceptable and CS has an FAQ for affected customers.

Communication & onboarding plan
- Weekly SLO standup (30m) during rollout weeks with owners, product, and observability.
- Office hours: SRE-led drop-in twice a week for instrumentation help and dashboard setup.
- Playbook & training: short recorded walkthroughs for adding route tags and mapping metrics to Console scorecards.
- Pilot cohort: 3 teams (Hosted API control plane, Dedicated autoscaler, Private control plane) + 2 customer pilots from Solutions for direct feedback.

Measurement of campaign health
- KPI dashboard (weekly): percent endpoints instrumented, percent endpoints with published SLO, mean time to acknowledge SLO alert, number of automated mitigations triggered, customer incidents attributed to SLO-managed flows.
- Success stories: publish two short case notes showing reduced incident duration or prevented customer impact via SLO automation.

Open questions & risks
- Telemetry costs: high-cardinality tags increase ingestion costs — need sampling and rollups strategy agreed with Finance.
- Model-quality SLIs: how to define a robust quality SLI for generation endpoints that balances false positives; work with Applied ML to propose proxy metrics.
- Cross-tenant fairness: SLOs at route level could mask per-tenant hotspots; plan a secondary per-tenant sampling to detect tenant-specific regressions.

Decision log (working notes)
- 2026-02-15: agreed minimal taxonomy (primary SLI + secondary SLI) and team responsibilities (Asha, Elena, Ravi).
- 2026-02-22: decided to prioritize Hosted API routes that serve model-initiated streaming and Dedicated control-plane endpoints.
- 2026-02-28: accepted downsample retention (raw 14d / rollup 90d) to control costs; revisit after pilot.

Next steps (immediate)
- Send intake form to product and service owners for endpoint nomination (due EOD +5 business days).
- Platform team to publish tag schema enforceable by ingestion agent (owner: Ravi) by Week 2.
- Observability to create a Console scorecard template and a dashboard stub for each pilot (owner: Elena).
- SRE to schedule weekly standups and office hours, publish meeting invite.

Appendix: quick templates
- SLO declaration (one-liner): service: <service-name> | primary SLI: <availability|latency P95> | target: <e.g., 99.95%/30d> | owner: <name> | tier: <customer|platform>.
- Runbook header: impact, detection signal, mitigation steps, rollback criteria, post-incident actions.

Approvals & sign-off
- Draft prepared by: Asha Mehta (SRE)
- Contributors: Liam O'Connor, Ravi Patel, Sofia Martinez, Elena Zhou, Marcus Bell
- Requesting review and approval from: Head of SRE (TBD), Head of Product (Hosted API), Head of Platform.

Notes to reviewers
- This campaign is intentionally lightweight: aim to create sustainable ownership patterns rather than a heavy centralized program. Expect follow-ups to refine metric definitions after the first pilot completes.
- Flag any dependencies on billing/finance for telemetry spend ASAP so we can scope sampling/retention appropriately.
